_note: Step-by-step clues for Clock (Chapter 10): the book questions and the past-paper questions filed under the chapter, by question id. Each list gives the speed of the hands (minute hand 6° a minute, hour hand 30° an hour and ½° a minute) or the rule for mirrors and gaining clocks, places both hands from 12, then sets up the last subtraction. The last clue never gives the answer. Questions marked needs-review have none. tools/check_clues.ts checks them.

cl-b01: The hour hand goes all the way round, 360°, in 12 hours. So it turns 360 ÷ 12 = 30° an hour.
From 9 in the morning to 3 in the afternoon is 6 hours.
cl-b02: Measure both hands from 12. The minute hand turns 6° a minute. The hour hand turns 30° an hour, plus ½° for every minute past the hour.
At 6:30 the hour hand is at 30 × 6 + ½ × 30 = 195°. The minute hand is at 6 × 30 = 180°. They are 15° apart.
The reflex angle is the big angle the other way round: 360° − 15° = ?
cl-b05: A mirror swaps left and right. The real time and the mirror time always add up to 12:00, so take the mirror time away from 11:60.
On a clock face, 0 o'clock is written as 12. So what is the real time?
cl-b06: Measure both hands from 12. The minute hand turns 6° a minute. The hour hand turns 30° an hour, plus ½° for every minute past the hour.
At 5:50 the hour hand is at 30 × 5 + ½ × 50 = 175°. The minute hand is at 6 × 50 = 300°.
cl-b07: Measure both hands from 12. The minute hand turns 6° a minute. The hour hand turns 30° an hour, plus ½° for every minute past the hour.
At 9:10 the hour hand is at 30 × 9 + ½ × 10 = 275°. The minute hand is at 6 × 10 = 60°. 275° − 60° = 215°.
215° is more than 180°, and 'the angle between the hands' means the smaller one: 360° − 215° = ?
cl-b08: Measure both hands from 12. The minute hand turns 6° a minute. The hour hand turns 30° an hour, plus ½° for every minute past the hour.
At 7:28 the hour hand is at 30 × 7 + ½ × 28 = 224°. The minute hand is at 6 × 28 = 168°. They are 56° apart.
The reflex angle is the big angle the other way round: 360° − 56° = ?
cl-b09: The watch gains 15 minutes in 24 hours, the same amount every hour.
From 12 noon to 4:00 am is 16 hours. In 16 hours it gains 15 × 16 ÷ 24 = 10 minutes.
The watch is 10 minutes fast. What does it show at 4:00 am?
cl-b10: The minute hand gains 5½ minute spaces on the hour hand every minute. To gain g spaces it takes g × 12/11 minutes.
At 6:00 the hour hand is at the 6, 30 minute spaces ahead of the minute hand.
To catch up 30 spaces takes 30 × 12/11 = 360/11 minutes. Write 360/11 as a mixed number: what time is it?
cl-b11: The minute hand gains 5½ minute spaces on the hour hand every minute. To gain g spaces it takes g × 12/11 minutes.
At 9:00 the hour hand is at the 9, 45 minute spaces ahead of the minute hand.
To catch up 45 spaces takes 45 × 12/11 = 540/11 minutes. Write 540/11 as a mixed number: what time is it?
